note: Lesson is a drill on awal / taani / aa5er / 8eir before vs after the noun; much of 17:00-48:00 is rule talk and listening drills. Rule hypotheses he states in English ('X means Y') with her 'Nothing'/'no' are treated as rule questions, not slips (17:53 and 21:50). 30:35-31:06 is ONE confusion (awal el-yoam vs el-yoam el-awal), kept once as D4.

row.medi_said: أنا لا مش شجاع اليوم. مش شجاع اليوم.
row.why: She asked لسه مش متشجع; he answered shujaa3 (brave), a different word with a different meaning, not a form of mitshajje3; she recast متشجع at 09:24.

rulings.why: Both readers agree on the slip; tier 1 because شجاع (brave) is a separate lexical item, not a wrong form of متشجع (motivated).

row.why: He stuck the my-ending -i onto 3ammo (3ammo-i); she recast عمي twice at 12:21/12:24 and he took it ('That's right'); first use at 11:24, repeated 12:18 - one row.

rulings.why: The fix is the possessive ending (A4: stick the owner on the end; -i on 3amm), not a different word; one row at the first use 11:24.

S4 pronunciation: for 13 he said 3asha(ra) dropping the r - a dropped letter of a number he knows (he said Ashra at 15:44, and 'talat 3ashar' is the date); her echo عشاء is a joke about the sound, not a vocab fix.

row.medi_said: الأول اليوم. ... The beginning of the day. ... الأول اليوم.
row.chat: awal el-sa3a = the beginning of the hour
row.why: Listening drill: she said أول اليوم and he repeated it as الأول اليوم (el- on the first word); she said 'Nothing' twice and gave اليوم الأول.

rulings.why: Real slip; mode is listening - it is her drill phrase أول اليوم that he repeated wrongly while translating, not his own sentence.

Not a clear slip: in her listening drill he said غير يوم first (right), then tried غير اليوم while thinking, and translated it right ('I'll see you another day'); her غير يوم repeats the drill phrase. The right form came before hers.

row.medi_said: Yes، uh، tan-- uh، تاني، تاني حدا.
row.amal_said: تاني حدا would mean the second person.
row.why: For 'someone else' the adjective taani must come after the noun; before it means 'second'. She said so and he accepted.

rulings.why: A7 fits exactly (adjective goes AFTER the noun); no PROPOSE needed.

row.amal_said: Yes. بس we learned how to say الأول for a feminine. What is it? Do you remember?
row.why: ساعة is feminine so the adjective is الأولى; she prompted for the feminine and he produced الساعة الأولى at 18:31.

rulings.why: He applied the after-the-noun pattern himself and used the masculine; she prompted, he fixed. A separate moment from A15 (28:43).

Rule hypothesis, not a use: 'and التاني الساعة means a different hour' is him testing the rule in English while she drills it (same as 17:53 'el awal elsaa ... I thought this was also the first hour', which neither reader counted); a question/hypothesis about the rule is neither a slip nor a use.
Duplicate of D4: 30:35-31:06 is one confusion between أول اليوم and اليوم الأول; the Arabic slip and her 'Nothing' are written as D4.

row.why: Listening: بيجي is present (b- present); he translated it as past, she nudged 'To come' and he changed to 'that comes' at 35:03.

rulings.why: Small but real listening slip: she voiced 'To come' and he took it; low because she also said 'Yeah, yeah'.

row.why: After the noun he used aa5er (the tool form) instead of the adjective a5eer that she taught at 32:17; she started ال أخي- and he switched to الأخير at the same second, so the order is unproven - low.

rulings.why: Distinct from A21 (which fixes the agreement of أخير to أخيرات); her ال أخي- reacts to his الآخر, but both are stamped 45:58, so low confidence.

challenges.why: Likely the engine: he said متأخر correctly at 07:04, ten seconds earlier, and تأخر is متأخر with the mi- dropped (near-sound). Amal's 08:35 'إنت صحيت متأخر و…' is her prompting him to go on, not a fix of 07:14 (a minute later). Needs audio.
Possibly the engine (من vs مش near-sound); right after, he asked 'Did I say it right?' and she said صح (53:08). Her 'Or مش نفس...' may offer an alternative rather than fix. Needs audio.
